summary: During the 2023 Turkey earthquakes, Google's Android Earthquake Alerts reportedly underestimated the first major quake and sent its highest-level warning to only 469 users. Researchers estimated about 10 million people could have received urgent alerts.
technical_summary: Android's crowdsourced earthquake detection uses phone accelerometers to estimate location and magnitude and choose an alert level. For the first magnitude-7.8 quake the system underestimated magnitude, so most recipients got a low-level notice instead of a screen-takeover warning, limiting warning time.

notes: Severity inferred: the quake killed over 50,000, but reports do not show how many deaths resulted from missed alerts. Google initially claimed the system worked.
